answer: Graph-conductance weighting resists sybils: an identitys trust kernel is the min-cut capacity between it and the honest seed core, not its local edge count. A sybil region attaches to the real graph through only a few attack edges, a narrow delta however dense its interior, so its conductance to the core is tiny and every fake inside shares that one bottleneck. Honest nodes sit behind wide, many-path cuts; a velvet-smooth internal mesh of clones adds no cut capacity across the chokepoint. Weight is bounded by the cut, so internal edge-spam buys nothing.
